subject: every scoring-relevant rule of the 2025 MSCA Doctoral Networks evaluation, read against the 2026 profile
purpose: The runbook proposes preparing a historical profile as a copy of the 2026 one, leaving a rule unchanged where no source states a difference. That is a defaulting policy, not evidence that the rule applied in 2025. This matrix replaces it: each rule is sourced to a 2025 document, or recorded as defaulted with the rule its defaulting affects, or recorded as an unresolved limitation. No verdict means that no difference was found.
declared_status_note: Inferred, not Confirmed. Every sourced row rests on a pinned document whose bytes nothing from an issuing body vouches for, and harness.authority_matrix.check refuses a Confirmed row on such a source.
supersedes: nothing. It is the first equivalence matrix on this branch. It supersedes no record and edits none: the specification's decision 3, which pinned one 2026 profile because the 2025 sources were absent, stands as written, and this matrix is what a historical profile is authored from instead.
uncertainties: Six rows are defaulted and two unresolved. All eight trace to the four unobtained 2025 documents, and five of them to the 2025 evaluation form alone.

A sourced row claims what its citations measure and no more. SM-01 compares the aspect anchors in both directions; AM-01 claims an inclusion only, so a 2025 cross-reference the 2026 mapping has no row for would not have been seen.

Whether an area's rows are all of its scoring-relevant rules is this author's judgement. The check reads what each row cites and refuses an unsourced relation; it cannot report a rule nobody wrote a row for.

The rows sourced to the 2025 evaluation's own record settle what was applied to this submission. None of them settles a rule of the 2025 call, and the check refuses a call-wide claim resting only on them.
EI-01, the six score-level descriptions, is the largest unsourced input to any numerical comparison with the 2025 result.

This matrix quotes the 2025 evaluation's recorded figures. It lives beside the ESR record, outside the dev-graph root, and is not snapshotted; the blind lane's isolation rests on that exclusion and on the assessor running with no tools from outside the repository, exactly as it does for the ESR record itself.
isolation_note: Written under docs/tier4_orchestration_state/msca_dn/, outside the dev-graph root at workspaces/msca_dn/. No snapshot reads it, so it cannot reach an evidence pack, which is the position the ESR record already holds (specification decision 12).
authority_note: This matrix confers no authority and closes no gate. It records what the sources state. A row marked defaulted is a declaration that a rule is unsourced, not a finding that it is wrong.

rows.historical_value: This file is not the text the ESR evaluated. It is a derivative produced by sanitisation after evaluation, and no result over it is a result over the submission.
rows.status_basis: The fidelity register states it over the file it pins by hash. This is a property of one derivative, measured on it.
rows.why_era_neutral: The candidate's fidelity is not a rule either call states. It is the condition of the document being assessed, and it bounds every row above regardless of which year's rules apply.
rows.consequence: No result over this copy is a result over the submission. The historical profile changes nothing about that, and a comparison with the 2025 total carries the statement.

rows.rule: A blind cell reports addressal and grounding as two values, and never blends them into one.
rows.current_value: two values per cell, grounding never folded into addressal
rows.status_basis: The specification's decision 4 states the rule and its reason. The citation resolves as text in the specification, so a reworded decision fails the check.
rows.why_era_neutral: What a cell reports is this harness's own output shape. Neither call states it, and neither could: no 2025 or 2026 document knows of a cell.
rows.consequence: The historical profile inherits the two-value cell. A reader comparing a cell with a 2025 criterion score is comparing an assessor's two axes with an evaluator's single grade, which this row records as a method difference rather than a rule difference.

citations.states: the specification's decision on what a blind cell reports

rows.rule: The criterion scorer reads the complete criterion section plus the declared appendix rows, with no selection and no budget filler.
rows.current_value: the whole section verbatim, within the 32,768-token pack budget, with every declared appendix row resolved
rows.status_basis: The specification states the input and its bound, and both citations resolve as text in it. What the scorer reads is a harness decision, not a call rule, which is why it is recorded here rather than compared across the two years.
rows.why_era_neutral: An evaluator reads the proposal. A pack budget and a selection rule are properties of the assessing harness, so no call document of either year states them.
rows.consequence: The historical profile inherits the input rule. A truncated or selected input would change a criterion score without any 2025 rule changing, which is why the bound is recorded as a scoring assumption and not left implicit.
